dmitri: quick dump from today's drop-in bench — fused-attn-tiling (v3) vs paged-attn-proto across A100/H100/L40S. ran seq lenses 128/512/2048/4096 and batch sizes 1/2/8. raw gist: H100 shows a 9-14% tail latency hump at seq=2048,batch=2 when tiled fusion is forced. attaching minimal logs below.

alex: can you paste the exact run command and the kernel selector flags?

dmitri: sure — ran with the usual harness: 
```bash
./bench_runner --model gpt2-like --hw=h100 --kernel-selector=tiling_fused_v3 --seqs="128,512,2048,4096" --batches="1,2,8" --kv-mode=online --enable-prefetch=true --runs=5
```
perf snippet (per-token median ms): 
```
H100 fused_v3 seq=2048 batch=2: 1.27 ms/token (baseline paged: 1.12 ms/token)
A100 fused_v3 seq=2048 batch=2: 1.34 ms/token (paged: 1.33 ms/token)
L40S fused_v3 seq=2048 batch=2: 1.85 ms/token (paged: 1.70 ms/token)
```

sophia: hmm that H100 delta is interesting. did you capture nvprof/ptp traces? could be memcpy thrash or kernel dispatch backlog.

perf-bot: pprof upload complete — flames at https://perf.internal/runs/2198765432

maria: I skimmed the flamegraph — lots of time in memcpy_async and a mid-launch gap aligning with KV writeback. looks like the tiled kernel path is triggering an extra KV flush for some interleaving pattern.

alex: what's different about fused_v3 tiling vs paged-proto here? I thought fused reduces mem copies by fusing q,k,v loads.

dmitri: v3 fuses but also introduces tiled prefetch windows that allocate a small staging buffer per threadblock. when sequence grows and batch>1 we see more staging-buffer churn. on H100 that maps to extra DMA sync calls.

sophia: any correlation with KV cache occupancy? if tile prefetch spills into CPU or triggers eviction policy that could explain latency spikes.

dmitri: good call. I replayed with kv-inspect logging. for that seq=2048,batch=2 case, kv cache hit drops ~3% and we see ~2.5x increase in eviction events per step. snippet: `kv_hits: 0.965 -> 0.935`, `evictions/sec: 12 -> 31`

maria: so tiled staging pushes active working set alignment off, causing slightly different key ordering -> more evictions. probably the kernel's prefetch stride interacts poorly with our LRU window.

alex: let's try a quick config toggle: run same bench with `--kernel-selector=tiling_fused_v3` but `--kv-prefetch-policy=conservative` and `--staging-size=small`. can you try?

dmitri: running now, will post numbers in a few.

ci-bot: triggered job 2198765432-tiling-prefetch-conservative on h100-pool (queue pos 2).

(45s later)

dmitri: conservative prefetch + smaller staging -> latency back down to 1.14 ms/token median on H100 at seq=2048,batch=2. kv_hits recovered to 0.962 and evictions/sec down to 14. so mitigation works but perf cost for smaller staging shows up at batch=8 where throughput drops ~6%.

sophia: tradeoff makes sense. this looks like a policy/heuristic issue, not a kernel bug per se. we should make kernel selector aware of kv working-set estimators.

maria: agreed. propose patch: selector consults recent kv_hit_rate and input-seq distribution; if hit_rate<0.95 and seq>1024 prefer paged-attn or fall back to fused but with conservative-prefetch. I can draft a PR.

alex: add a microbenchmark that simulates KV churn (randomized key sequences) so we don't regress this silently. also add a perf test gating for H100 tail latency.

dmitri: filing issue and including benchmark matrix + attach pprof link: https://perf.internal/issue/RED-3142. I'll start a bisect on recent selector commits to see if a change amplified the effect.

perf-bot: bisect job queued -> https://ci.internal/bisect/2198765432 (estimated 14 runs).

sophia: next steps: 1) temporary heuristic change (selector) 2) microbench with kv-churn 3) instrumentation: add counters for staging allocations and DMA syncs 4) long-run (24h) to catch rare tails.

maria: I'll take the selector patch. dmitri can you own the microbench and perf gating?

dmitri: yep. will push a small canary flag `--force-staging-size=auto` defaulting to conservative for now. thanks all :thumbsup:
